text:
Former Vice President and Presidential Candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, says the Tinubu administration is making Nigeria too expensive to produce in, too expensive to build in and too expensive for ordinary families to live in.
Atiku, in a statement issued by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, said reports that just 11 listed manufacturers spent ₦842 billion on energy in the first nine months of 2026 expose the cost of the government’s failure to provide dependable, affordable power.
“₦842 billion is the energy bill of only 11 companies in nine months. Cement manufacturers are among the industries hit hardest by the cost of power. That cost does not disappear at the factory gate. It enters the price of every bag of cement and pushes the cost of building a home further beyond the reach of ordinary Nigerians.
“It is laughable that a government under which cement has become so expensive now boasts of producing more houses for Nigerians. How does it expect families to afford those houses when its energy failures make the materials used to build them more costly? This contradiction exposes the deception that has become a hallmark of the Tinubu administration.”
Atiku said the manufacturers’ reported 7.4 per cent increase in energy spending over the same period in 2025 was a warning about the wider economy.
“When factories spend fortunes on electricity, diesel and gas, they raise prices, cut production, postpone expansion or shed jobs. Families then pay more for everything those factories produce. Tinubu’s energy failure is being added to every Nigerian’s bill.”
Atiku said the APC Presidential Campaign Council’s claim that the administration has delivered more than 26,000 housing units deserves the same scrutiny. Its own statement includes 10,328 units still under construction, while its project list includes Federal Housing Authority sites that were under way during the Buhari administration.
“A building site is not a completed home. An inherited project is not proof of fresh delivery. A mortgage approval is not a house key. Publish what Tinubu inherited, what his administration completed, how many families have moved in and what those homes cost.”
He also challenged the APC to provide evidence for its claim of 525,100 construction jobs, saying estimated employment opportunities should not be announced as jobs already created.
Atiku said his Affordable Life campaign would address the costs that make both goods and homes unaffordable: unreliable power, expensive production and fuel prices that spread through the economy. His administration would prioritise dependable electricity for industry and a transparent, targeted subsidy for domestically refined fuel, with relief Nigerians can measure at the pump.
“You cannot build affordable homes with cement that families and builders can no longer afford. You cannot protect jobs while factories spend fortunes generating their own power. And you cannot restore purchasing power by calling hardship reform.
“Tinubu’s campaign can count unfinished houses and estimated jobs. Nigerians are counting what it costs to keep the lights on, buy food, purchase cement and pay rent. Bring down the cost of production. Hand over homes people can afford. Make Nigeria affordable again.”
